text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Media should be vigilant about Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, Information Minister Sheikh Saud Nasser al-Sabah says. Kuwait says Iraq still has "aggrresive intentions" towards the Gulf Arab state. Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990 and annexed its for seven months until a U.S.-led coalition ejected Iraq's troops.
- Kuwait hails Britain's position towards former occupier Iraq.
- Crown prince and prime minister received message from Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.
- Investment firms lead active trade at the Kuwait Stock Exchange, index hits peak.
- Kuwait hands over 11 wanted Egyptians to Cairo.
- Commerce and industry ministry is looking into a law to allow foriegners to trade in Kuwaiti shares, bourse official.

- Former oil minister Sheikh Ali al-Khalifa al-Sabah asks court to dismiss fraud case. Sheikh Ali faces charges of making illegal profits from the operations of Kuwait Oil Tanker Company (KOTC). He denies any wrongdoing.
